item.title: Airbnb founder Chesky donates $100 million to San Francisco parks
item.description: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky has donated $100 million to San Francisco's parks, the largest gift from an individual donor in the city's history. The announcement was made alongside Mayor Daniel Lurie last week in Golden Gate Park. Chesky founded Airbnb 18 years ago in San Francisco, where the company remains headquartered. item.title: SpaceX catches Starship with mechanical arms and makes history
item.description: SpaceX has for the first time caught a Starship spacecraft with mechanical arms at its launch facility in Texas, 22 hours after launch. According to the company, this demonstrates Starship's full reusability, intended for trips to the moon and Mars. The first-stage booster exploded shortly after launch on Friday, preventing the hoped-for double catch. SpaceX had previously successfully caught a...

item.title: Couple with autism and ADHD clean dirty street signs in Brighton
item.description: Paul and Ruth Richmond-Watson from Brighton, England, have been cleaning dirty street signs in East Sussex since September. The couple, both autistic with ADHD, were looking for a hobby to do together. Paul (47), originally from New Zealand and a former window cleaner, and Ruth (25) clean at least one sign per day, which takes each 20 to 25 minutes...

item.title: Ada Le Poidevin hid British soldiers from Nazis on Guernsey
item.description: The heroic wartime deeds of British shopkeeper Ada Le Poidevin have come to light 40 years after her death. During the Second World War, she and her husband Walter hid three British commandos — corporal Dennis Dumper, soldier Fred Drain and soldier Andrew Ross — in their garden shed on Nazi-occupied Guernsey, despite German troops living next door. item.title: Atolls Bikar and Bokak become new marine reserve
item.description: In the Marshall Islands, the coral atolls Bikar and Bokak have been designated as part of the country's first national marine reserve. Scientists describe the two remote atolls, located between Hawaii and the Philippines, as one of the last virtually pristine ecosystems in the world. item.description: Rick Addante from Palm Bay, Florida, rescued his vulnerable neighbors during a flood he himself described as 'biblical'. On Monday, between 16 and 22 inches of rain fell in a single day, part of what is being called a 1,000-year rainfall event. item.title: PolyGone Systems microplastics filter launches in Atlantic City
item.description: A water treatment facility in Atlantic City, New Jersey, has become the first in the world to be equipped with a system that removes microplastics from wastewater before it enters the ocean. item.title: China switches on world's largest liquid-air battery
item.description: In China's Qinghai province, the world's largest demonstration facility for liquid-air energy storage (LAES) has been put into operation. The installation uses green electricity to compress air to extreme density, after which it becomes liquid at approximately -190°C. item.description: After 100 years, Gretchen Sollo experienced her first birthday celebration, organized by employees of Lowe's in Bradley, Illinois. item.title: Brown bear population in Spain doubles thanks to protection
item.description: The Cantabrian brown bear has doubled in number over twenty years: from around 140 animals at the start of this century to 370 now. The bears no longer live exclusively in Cantabria, but also in Asturias, León, Galicia and Palencia, across an area of more than 17,000 square kilometres (6,500 square miles). A 2023 study in Conservation Science and Practice...

item.title: Brazil presents world's first fossil fuel phase-out roadmap
item.description: Brazil has become the first country in the world to publish a roadmap for phasing out fossil fuels. The document marks a unique step in international climate policy, making Brazil the first nation to publicly release such a concrete phase-out plan.

item.description: Flag football, long seen as an alternative to tackle football, is gaining strong popularity among girls. According to USA Football, participation by girls aged 6 to 17 has risen 57% over the past decade, reaching over 267,000 participants in 2024. item.title: Italy invests $2.2 million in fighting dog rescue
item.description: Italy has allocated 2 million euros (approximately $2.2 million) to rescue dogs from illegal dogfighting operations and help them recover. The funds will go to shelters and rehabilitation facilities that provide care and behavioral training, enabling traumatized dogs to be rehomed with families.
